Only SO (on 'GPIO10', pin 16) matches. The whole CS0/SCK/CS1/CS2 group is shifted one GPIO low relative to the intended mapping.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the firmware drives SCK on GPIO5, SO on GPIO10, and the three chip-selects CS0/CS1/CS2 on GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7 respectively (TL;DR: 'SPI2 on GPIO5/GPIO10, CS pins GPIO4/6/7'; §4: 'U1 GPIO5/SCK, GPIO10/SO ... driven by ESP32 GPIO4/GPIO6/GPIO7'). The schematic should place SCK on the GPIO05 pin, CS0 on GPIO04, CS1 on GPIO06, CS2 on GPIO07.

anomalies.impact: The firmware's SPI2 thermocouple bus is mis-routed: the SCK net sits on the GPIO the firmware treats as CS0, CS0 sits on an unassigned GPIO3, CS1/CS2 sit one GPIO low, and the intended CS2 GPIO7 is floating. Sequential polling of the three MAX31855s would clock the wrong line, assert the wrong (or no) chip-select, and leave one thermocouple permanently deselected, breaking all temperature reads and the heater control loop.

parsed.summary: Anomaly detected: the SPI bus control nets (SCK, CS0, CS1, CS2) on U1 are connected to GPIOs that are each one position lower than the firmware/specification mapping (SCK on GPIO4 instead of GPIO5, CS0 on GPIO3 instead of GPIO4, CS1 on GPIO5 instead of GPIO6, CS2 on GPIO6 instead of GPIO7, with GPIO7 left unconnected), so the thermocouple SPI interface would not function as intended. The power, heater, USB, fan and regulator sections otherwise match the specification.
